evidence.claim: Probe 1 enumerated allow/deny in every Claude and Cursor settings scope, computed the live merged set, and showed on a three-scope fixture that local Bash(rm *) deny removes the project allow of the same rule.

question: Which command patterns are pre-approved in the permissions allow-lists across all settings scopes, and which of those would let a caller bypass a hook that is supposed to gate them?

answer.summary: Live Claude settings files present: project-claude (empty permissions.allow on each). Live Cursor user scope effective allow is Shell(ls); project Cursor cli.json is absent. Live settings files with parseable JSON: ['project-claude', 'user-cursor']. No live hook matchers are configured, so no live allow entry can bypass a live hook — there is no hook to skip. Catalog tool_policy is a related program allow/deny list and was not merged into the live settings set (scope-mismatch). Fixture merge shows deny wins: Bash(rm *) is allowed at project scope and stripped by local deny.
